newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index dives at noon on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index dives at noon on profit-taking.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index took a fall on Tuesday morning when investors returning from a three-day break sold heavily after last week's sharp gains, brokers said.
The hard currency index ended the morning down 9.35 points, or 5.89 percent, to 149.37 on turnover of HK$188.5 million.
"Investors cashed in after last Thursday's and Friday's phenomenal speculative buying," a trader at J&A Securities said.

A shift of focus to the B shares last week from the more expensive H shares, or shares listed in Hong Kong by mainland companies, drove the B index to a rare 10 percent limit-up close on Thursday and a strong performance on Friday.
Shenzhen's B share market was closed on Monday in line with a public holiday in Hong Kong.
Heavy losses in the Hong Kong market also weighed down the B index, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index was down more than three percent by midday.
Analysts said the B index could narrow losses in the afternoon, when investors picked up shares now considered undervalued.
Investors were, however, ambivalent about the debut of Luthai Textile Joint Stock Co Ltd, which rose to HK$2.48 by midday from the issue price of HK$1.93, becoming the only stock to rise.
Some analysts had said they expected Luthai's 80 million B shares to trade on the first day at between HK$3.0 and HK$4.0.
"When predictions were made last week for Luthai's debut, most people were not expecting such a sharp market fall," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
Property concern Hainan Pearl River Enterprises Co Ltd was one of the biggest losers and fell to its 10 percent limit-down level of HK$2.16.

The A index, however, ended the morning at 367.64 points, up 0.59 percent on turnover of 1.0 billion yuan, after market-leader Shenzhen Development Bank said it would go ahead with its original dividend plan based on 1996 profits.
The company's stocks tumbled when it was recently punished for trading its own shares. At Tuesday midday, it rose 0.93 yuan to 31.44 yuan.
